chunks: From him, from Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣabbāḥ, who said:

I wrote to al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام: “The disk disappears, night approaches, then the night continues to rise, the sun becomes hidden from us, and a redness rises above the night, while the mu'adhdhins call the adhan in our area. Should I perform salat (prayer) at that time and break my fast if I am fasting, or should I wait until the redness that is above the night goes away?”
So he wrote back to me: “I hold that you should wait until the redness goes away, and take precaution for your religion.”

key_terms.الْحَائِطَةِ: precaution and safeguarding in religious practice
key_terms.الْعَبْدِ الصَّالِحِ: a title used for the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.حُمْرَةٌ: the red twilight glow remaining after sunset

ai.seo_question: Should one pray maghrib and break the fast as soon as the sun sets, or wait until the twilight redness disappears?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the time of maghrib and iftar when twilight redness remains after the sun's disk has disappeared. The Imam عليه السلام instructs waiting until the redness disappears, emphasizing precaution in matters of religion.
